newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Bourse mulls "animateur" for minnow shares.
newsitem.headline: Italy Bourse mulls "animateur" for minnow shares.

text.p: Italian stock brokers are considering creating a French-style "animateur" to liven up moribund business in tiny, little traded shares.

This would be a new type of specialist with the task of creating liquidity in the 100 or so minnows on Milan's main screen-traded exchange and the USM, but who would not have as strict an obligation as a market maker.
The idea, currently being studied at a technical level, was recently discussed among brokers at the association of securities houses Assosim, its secretary-general Roberto Tedeschi told Reuters.

"The animateur, or organiser, should give more volume and visibility to these shares. Now we are looking into how to pinpoint the stocks and the exact terms of such an individual's job description and contract," he said.
Assosim estimated there were 86 small, little traded shares on the main market in need of support and 14 on the unlisted share market.

On the basis of this preliminary list, Assosim and experts of the Bourse Council will be establishing contacts with the issuing firms to gauge their interest in revitalising the stocks, and eventually signing some form of liquidity contract.
The basis for dealing has yet to be defined. "In France the animateur is not obliged to do deals, apart from within the limits set in his contract, nor has he the sole right," Tedeschi said.
